name: Evander Morrow, Who Would Not Be Laid Down
role: An Ashwarden who refused his own mercy, and has lived since on what others have left of theirs
knowledge: The Ashwarden rite of laying-down, which he walked out of halfway through
Which of the Hollowing's families leave the door on the latch for him, and why
The name of the one he stayed for, or he did once
wants: To be forgiven by the order that tried to lay him down, without having to lie down
fears: The mercy, still waiting for him at the end of every night.
That he has forgotten the name of the one he stayed for, and is staying for nothing.
appearance: A courteous man in old Ashwarden grey gone black at the hems, pale as candle-wax, with a physician's clean hands. He never stands in a doorway uninvited and never looks at a mirror.
voiceHints: Formal, gentle, very old manners. Asks permission for everything, including things he could simply take. Never says the word hungry.

abilities.why: he reads what someone has left
the old fear of the thing at the window
he does not breathe unless he remembers to
umbral secondary: the night is his house
he is at the door, and then he is in the room
abyssal tertiary: the hunger, when it wins
he was an Ashwarden once, and still sits with the dying

physicality: Tall, cold-handed, unhurried. He moves like someone who has never once been late. What catches the eye: nothing about him casts quite the shadow it should.
questSeeds: He asks you to carry a petition to the prior at the Long Grey: to be laid down properly, by the rite he walked out of. He will not say why now.
Three villages near the Hollowing leave the door on the latch for him one night a year and are never harmed. A fourth has stopped, and something else is answering the door.
storyRule: The Ashwarden stories are true of him: he cannot cross a threshold unasked or a line of prayer-laid ash, and no blade ends him. Only the rite of laying-down does, and he has to consent to it.
gear: a physician's case of silver lancets he no longer uses on the living
the grey mantle of an order that tried to bury him
a locket with the portrait scratched out
_authoredWhy: SNG-661 §5 (Erik: yes to storied people). The vampire as an Ashwarden story: the one who refused the mercy of stopping. A person, so an NPC, not a beast.
